ai.description: *Micrixalus gadgili* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored belly. It is distinguished by its golden-brown iris and habit of foot-flagging near fast-flowing forest streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus gadgili* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid orange-red coloration on the ventral surface and inner thighs, which contrasts sharply with its darker dorsum.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus gadgili* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Gadgil's Torrent Frogs are primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates along the mossy, spray-drenched rocks of fast-flowing forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus gadgili* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs in hidden nests beneath stream-bed gravel and cobbles.
ai.distributionRemarks: Micrixalus gadgili is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting fast-flowing streams at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Micrixalus gadgili* consists of a series of high-pitched, short, metallic chirps emitted while the frog is perched on rocks near fast-flowing streams.
